newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet shares at year-low as board meets.
newsitem.headline: Eramet shares at year-low as board meets.

text.p: Shares in nickel producer Eramet hit a year-low on Tuesday amid speculation chairman Yves Rambaud may leave the company if a proposed change in the group's legal status goes through, dealers and analysts said on Tuesday.
Eramet was off 11 francs at 255 francs at 0834 GMT.

Eramet officials said state-controlled holding company Erap had called a board meeting on Tuesday to study a plan to turn Eramet into a company with supervisory and management boards. The meeting started at 0700 GMT, they said.
If cleared, the proposal would allow a change in leadership.

Rambaud opposes plans by local groups in New Caledonia, a French territory, and Canadian firm Falconbridge to build a nickel plant in northern New Caledonia which would compete with Eramet's mines there, analysts said.

The plan, which is supported by the French government - Eramet's main shareholder - would deal a blow to Eramet's expansion strategy in New Caledonia as Eramet would have to part with some of the reserves of its Thiebaghi nickel deposit.
Eramet ranks third among world nickel producers. It plans to produce more than 60,000 tonnes of nickel by the year 2,000, up from expected 1996 output of 53,000 tonnes.
The higher output is expected to come mostly from nickel facilities in New-Caledonia, where the company recently decided to build a fifth rotary kiln at its Doniambo smelter.
Eramet started to develop the Thiebaghi nickel deposit in early 1995 and hoped to eventually reach capacity of 24,000 tonnes of nickel.
Analysts said the government's controversial stance also raised concern among investors about how the French state treats minority investors and may have an impact on future privatisations.
"This shows how much the French government cares about minority interests," one analyst told Reuters.
